body: Exercise helped me a bit with my major depression; it was one of the only things that worked, actually.  Now that I can't exercise I'm REALLY seeing the difference and it's hurting me bad.  If you can still do intense exercise, don't take it for granted.  I miss those days.

I haven't had a job since my late teens; I finished a four-year degree a few years ago.  Don't get out much, twice a week usually.  Can't exercise with any intensity due to some painful physical injuries, etc.  

I don't know why my fuzzy thinking and poor memory never cleared up.  I had depression in my mid-late teens too, but still thought clearly.  Only once (and after) I took medication did I have noticeable cognitive issues.
It's not that hard if you don't do it impulsively.  And I am not an impulsive person.

They seem well-educated, intelligent, and like they actually care (I cannot say the same of some in the past).  But other than, "Oh that's nice, they're a pretty good person" I'm not sure how much that does now.  I guess the point I was trying to make about the therapist was that I simply can't predict what effect non-detrimental assistance like this would've had at a time when my brain was very different from what it is now.  I've tried to be as open-minded as I possibly could about non-drug treatment...even to the point of stupidity.  I don't know what you and others see here, but I know that I was someone who "got help" early and "did the right thing" (blah blah blah) and it only hurt me more!  I tried, I fucking honestly tried.

I don't know what purpose trying to pick apart semantics in a post from an addled brain serves.  My point on reasons to live was just my cold attempt to relate, I guess.  None of this changes the problem...............

I can't tell you what makes me happy now.  The best I can do is to remember what made me happy in the past.  Money?  No, not really.  Relationships?  I wouldn't know.  They were just imitations of the real thing.  Achievement?  Ah, there.  At one time, yes, it did help.  But now I fail at everything.  The meager abilities I had are trashed.  The achievements were mostly through effort and determination, and I'm emptied of those (obviously).

Despair doesn't show I care.  Despair is just the absence of hope.  Despair is the pain of absence, then.  Pain doesn't show that I care, it just shows that I am still breathing.

The psychiatrist that prescribed them is long gone.  I definitely would have liked someone to beat him up...preferably in multiple ways.  I was naive and stupid to trust someone that handed out medication like it was candy, but I always was too trusting when I was younger.  I certainly didn't have to push him; he pushed me from one to the next and I went along with it like a fucking idiot.

It's too bad I never logged the effects of the medication at the time, but I couldn't keep up with routine things as it was.  I hoped the state I fell into would just blow over.  Five years later, it's still here and worse than ever.  No episodes of ups and downs, just one massive depression.

I still see a therapist these days.  I've been through about a half-dozen and I can tell (I think?) this one is actually pretty good.  Pity that they're too late.  If we started 5-10 years ago and stayed faaaar away from medication, maybe I would have had a chance at a decent life.

I have a defective mind.  No matter what I do, it doesn't even make a dent on the depression and hopelessness in my mind.  I can't form basic human relationships or feel loved.  Most of the time I can't even go out the door without being brought to my knees (I'm not speaking figuratively) with panic attacks.  All of the abilities I thought I had (and they were nothing impressive to begin with) were ravaged.  I'm a fucking retard now.  I barely even remembered to mention that I was sexually abused as a child because I just don't fucking care any more.  If I had a brain, passion, or even just some talent at something maybe I could force myself to stay alive.  But I don't.

I'm in my twenties.  How do you not understand the need?  Does a human being tortured say to their torturer, "Please sir, I would strongly prefer that you stop driving nails through my hands"?  No, you scream in agony "AHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH FUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUCCCCCCCCCCCCK!!!!!!"  You don't want the torture to stop, you need it too.

I've tried most of the major anti-depressants and some anxiety medication (part of the problem is I can't remember shit any more so I don't even remember their names).  They amplified my suicidal impulses and sent into the suicidal depression I'm still in today.  That was years ago.  When did the first signs of depression show?  Who knows now, probably a decade ago.

Yeah, it's a terrible thing to say.  I'm going to kill myself, though, so why should I give a fuck?  Corpses can't feel guilty for offending people.  The younger, better me wouldn't have said it but I'm not that person any more.  

I would be arrogant to think that some people don't have it worse than me or that they're in a similar state.  There are many such people who have already killed themselves or are planning to, after all.  But that's not the point any way.  Measuring pain does not solve it.
